summary: XRD analysis of CsPbBr3 nanocrystals synthesized with varying oleic acid (OlA) to oleylamine (Oleym) ratios reveals that the main perovskite phase is preserved across most ligand conditions, but secondary CsPb2Br5 phase emerges at high OlA content.

key_findings.finding: CsPbBr3 nanocrystals exhibit consistent XRD peak positions and narrow peak widths across OlA:Oleym ratios from 0.1:0.9 to 0.7:0.3, indicating phase purity and high crystallinity.
At higher OlA:Oleym ratios (0.8:0.2 and 0.9:0.1), additional peaks corresponding to CsPb2Br5 appear alongside CsPbBr3, indicating the formation of a secondary phase.

scientific_interpretation: The XRD results suggest that the structural phase of CsPbBr3 nanocrystals is stable over a wide range of capping ligand ratios, but excessive oleic acid (OlA) promotes the formation of CsPb2Br5 as a secondary phase. This implies that ligand composition critically influences phase purity: maintaining a balanced or Oleym-rich environment favors single-phase CsPbBr3, while high OlA content destabilizes the perovskite structure, leading to phase segregation. The consistently narrow peaks across all samples indicate good crystallinity, regardless of phase composition.
limitations: Only one XRD figure is provided, limiting cross-figure comparison.
No quantitative phase fraction or crystallite size analysis is reported.
Peak intensities and relative phase abundances are not discussed.
No information on how structural changes correlate with optoelectronic properties within the XRD data.
Absence of explicit lattice parameter refinement or detailed structural modeling.
